findings.issue: The imported P128 analysis helpers were not initially bound by the new analyzer single-file hash.
findings.resolution: The exact fixed P128 helper SHA is checked against both disk and the fixed baseline before and after analysis; both analyzers are also included in the child producer source identity.

findings.issue: A nonfinite kappa could produce a failed rate helper result but then throw in the later paired interval before the whole-analysis failure report was written.
findings.resolution: The complete per-timestep cohort is now screened before inference; all rows and exact nonfinite field paths/representations are retained, inference is unavailable, no kappa CSV is written, and the pass flag is false. Finite nonpositive kappa is also retained without log-rate inference.

limitations: This is not a P256 scientific result or a second execution record for root-owned tests.
The child scheduling coordinator still requires a separate exclusion/admission/drain review before any long child launch.
Intervals are nominal, are not sequentially adjusted, and do not bound arbitrary rare recrossing or PES/model uncertainty.
A sampled boundary minimum is not an every-step distance guarantee; the report distinguishes it from native hard guards and full-Hamiltonian extrema.
reviewer: providers subagent; independent read-only code and statistical review
verified_contracts: All eight registered seeds, both timesteps and both two-pair batches must complete before inference.
Each chain uses the exact bound parent checkpoint/normalization/source identity and both timesteps must have identical keyed momenta and equivalent-channel hashes.

The P256 reactant row is selected explicitly and checked against the fixed P256 log ratio, reduced mass, free-kernel beta, temperature, domain and PES identity. The P128 finite-P denominator is not substituted.
Same-chain log(Z_TS) and log(kappa) are combined before the within-group variance, retaining their covariance.
The P256 and P128 groups are independent eight-chain groups. Welch uses s256^2/8+s128^2/8, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, and mean(log k256)-mean(log k128).
Full-rate equivalence requires the entire two-sided 95% interval inside plus/minus log(1.05); the corresponding ratio band is [1/1.05,1.05].
Within-P256 time/timestep controls retain paired-chain 95% intervals, df = 7, and the unchanged 0.01 absolute margins. The parent-time-half 0.03 diagnostic remains explicitly supplementary.
The 76,800,000 total native-step check equals 8 chains × 200 parents × 4 pairs × 2 signs × 200 frames × (10+20 steps/frame). Individual children do not become uncertainty units.
The adapter source identity revision adds the analysis dependencies only. Its propagation/RNG/checkpoint suffix and summary statistical body remain AST-identical to the frozen P128 implementation.
